title: Bethlehem Central Senior High School reports 52 multiracial students for 2025-26
text:
Bethlehem Central Senior High School had 52 multiracial students enrolled during the 2025-26 school year, reflecting a 33.3% increase from the prior year, according to the New York State Education Department .
Records indicate the school’s total enrollment reached 1,306 students for 2025-26. Of that number, multiracial students made up 4% of the population, ranking as the third least represented ethnic group at the school.
The campus is part of Bethlehem Central School District, which has its main office in Delmar.
Within the district’s seven schools, Bethlehem Central Middle School had the highest number of multiracial students at the time, totaling 57 students.
New York is second in the nation for K-12 public education spending , with current expenditures averaging $30,012 per student, nearly twice the national average of $16,526, the Education Data Initiative reports.
